questions.question: How many languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India lists the official languages recognized by the Indian government.
 
• Originally, the Constitution of India recognized 14 languages under the Eighth Schedule.
 
• The number of languages has been increased to 22 by subsequent amendments, with the latest additions being Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali.
 
• These languages are given a special status and recognition, and the government promotes the development and usage of these languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitution of India**

 
 
• The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India, laying down the framework that defines the political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and duties of citizens.
 
• It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on 26 November 1949 and became effective on 26 January 1950.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Schedule**
 
 
• The Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India lists the official languages recognized by the Indian government.
 
• It initially included 14 languages: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu.
 
• Subsequent amendments have added Sindhi (21st Amendment, 1967), Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali (71st Amendment, 1992), Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (92nd Amendment, 2003).
 
 
 
• **Official Languages of India**
 
 
• India does not have a national language.
 
• However, the Constitution of India designates Hindi in the Devanagari script and English as the official languages of the Union to be used for official purposes.
 
• The states and union territories of India can have their own official languages based on their linguistic demographics.
 
 
 
• **Language Promotion**
 
 
• The Government of India promotes the development and usage of the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.
 
• This includes measures to ensure their propagation, preservation, and protection.
 
• The Sahitya Akademi, a national organization, supports literature in these languages.

questions.question: Which of the following structures of a plant is responsible for transpiration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stomata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transpiration**

 
 
• **It is a process in which excess water is lost in the form of vapors from the aerial parts of the plant.**
 
• **Mainly through the stomates of leaves. Hence, Option 3 is correct.**
 
• Stomatal openings are necessary to admit carbon dioxide to the leaf interior and to allow oxygen to escape during photosynthesis, hence transpiration is generally considered to be merely an unavoidable phenomenon that accompanies the real functions of the stomates.
 
• It has been proposed that transpiration provides the energy to transport water in the plant and may aid in heat dissipation in direct sunlight (by cooling through the evaporation of water), though these theories have been challenged.
 
• **Excessive transpiration can be extremely injurious to a plant. **
 
• **When water loss exceeds water intake, it can retard the plant’s growth and ultimately lead to death by dehydration.**
 
• The stomata present in the leaves are responsible for the uptake of carbon dioxide and limit the loss of water due to evaporation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The xylem of a plant** is the system of tubes and transport cells that circulates water and dissolved minerals.
 
• **The roots of a plant** anchor the plant to the ground, absorb water and nutrients from the soil and store reserve food for the plant.
 
• **Bark **protects the tree’s inner layers from insects and fungi and bacteria and also against water loss and predators.

questions.question: When is the World no Tobacco day celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**May 31.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **World No Tobacco Day** is observed annually on **May 31** to raise awareness about the harmful effects of tobacco usage and advocate for effective policies to reduce tobacco consumption.
 
• The day was established by the **World Health Organization (WHO)** in 1987 to draw global attention to the tobacco epidemic and its lethal consequences.
 
• Each year, World No Tobacco Day has a specific theme; for example, the 2023 theme focused on "**Grow food, not tobacco**" to promote sustainable agriculture and discourage tobacco farming.
 
• Governments and organizations worldwide use this day to launch anti-tobacco campaigns, host educational events, and implement stricter regulations on tobacco products.
 
• Smoking-related illnesses kill over **8 million people annually**, and this initiative seeks to reduce these alarming numbers through education and advocacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tobacco and Health Impacts:**

 
 
• Tobacco usage is a major cause of **cardiovascular diseases, cancers, and respiratory disorders**.
 
• Exposure to secondhand smoke is equally harmful, causing **1.2 million deaths annually** worldwide.
 
 
 
• **WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC):**
 
 
• Adopted in 2003, it is the first international treaty focused on controlling tobacco consumption.
 
• The treaty outlines measures like **taxation, advertising bans, and public smoking restrictions** to curb tobacco usage.
 
 
 
• **Economic Burden of Tobacco:**
 
 
• Tobacco use imposes a significant economic burden on healthcare systems due to the treatment of tobacco-related illnesses.
 
• It also affects productivity, as tobacco-related diseases lead to **premature deaths and disabilities**.
 
 
 
• **Global Campaigns:**
 
 
• Various organizations, including WHO, run campaigns like "**Quit Tobacco**" to encourage smokers to stop using tobacco products.
 
• Anti-tobacco ads, public service announcements, and support programs aim to reduce tobacco dependency worldwide.

questions.question: When a metal and sulphuric acid react with each other, metal displaces hydrogen, which is higher in the reactivity series. Identify the metal for which the bubbling of hydrogen gas will be the fastest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnesium is higher in the reactivity series compared to Iron, Aluminium, and Zinc.
 
• When magnesium reacts with sulphuric acid, it displaces hydrogen gas rapidly due to its high reactivity.
 
• The reactivity series of metals places magnesium above zinc, iron, and aluminium, making it more reactive.
 
• Hydrogen gas bubbles will form at a faster rate when magnesium is used in the reaction with sulphuric acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:** The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity to displace hydrogen from acids and water.
 
• **Hydrogen Displacement:** Metals higher in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen gas from acids faster than those lower in the series.
 
• **Magnesium (Mg):** A lightweight, silvery metal that reacts vigorously with acids to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• **Sulphuric Acid (H₂SO₄):** A strong acid commonly used in chemical reactions to test the reactivity of metals.
 
• **Safety Precautions:** When performing reactions with acids, appropriate safety measures like wearing gloves and goggles should be taken to prevent harm.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not an instrument of selective credit control in India?
questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

__
 
• When Reserve Bank controls the flow of credit to a certain sector of the economy and can be imposed for various goals like discouraging hoarding and black-marketing of certain essential commodities etc by giving them less credit.
 
• Either credit can be rationed or interest rate can be hiked by RBI for certain sectors as a part of SCCs.
 
• In SCCs, the total quantum of credit does not change.
 
• 
 
**Regulation of Consumer Credit:** This is a selective credit control measure aimed at controlling the amount and terms of credit extended to consumers for the purchase of durable goods. By regulating consumer credit, the central bank can influence consumer spending and manage inflation.

 
 
• 
 
**Rationing of Credit:** This is another selective credit control measure where the central bank restricts the amount of credit that banks can extend to certain sectors or borrowers. This helps in controlling the credit flow to specific areas of the economy.

 
 
• 
 
**Margin Requirement:** Margin requirements refer to the minimum amount that a borrower must provide as their own contribution when taking a loan, particularly in the context of purchasing securities or commodities. By adjusting margin requirements, the central bank can influence the volume of credit extended for speculative activities.

 
 
• 
 
**Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF): This is not an instrument of selective credit control. LAF is a tool used by the Reserve Bank of India to manage liquidity and ensure stability in the financial system. It involves operations like repo and reverse repo transactions, which are used to adjust the liquidity conditions in the banking system on a daily basis. LAF is a part of quantitative credit control measures rather than selective credit control.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The central bank (Reserve Bank of India in the context of India) uses these measures to achieve various economic objectives, such as controlling inflation, managing liquidity, and ensuring financial stability.
 
• There are two main types of credit control.
 
• **Quantitative Credit Control:** These measures regulate the overall volume of credit in the economy. Examples include bank rate policy, open market operations, and variations in the cash reserve ratio (CRR) and statutory liquidity ratio (SLR).
 
• **Selective Credit Control (SCC): **These measures target specific sectors of the economy to control the flow of credit. They are used to channelize credit into priority areas and curb excessive lending to speculative or non-productive sectors.

Thus, D is the correct answer
